nodes.content: Infer calibrated cell ancestry from incomplete lineage barcodes and transcriptional states despite state convergence and biased lineage sampling.
requirements: Improve ancestral-pair AUROC by ≥0.05 over barcode-only inference with 30% barcode dropout.
Achieve ancestry-probability expected calibration error ≤0.05 under convergent states and uneven lineage sampling.

nodes.content: Fit a dropout-aware barcode–expression ancestry model with convergent-state mixtures, lineage-sampling propensities, and inverse-propensity-weighted isotonic calibration.
How can the model distinguish convergent transcriptional similarity from shared ancestry when 30% barcode dropout conceals inherited edits?
State-mixture adjustment and posterior inherited-edit gating yield ≥0.05 ancestral-pair AUROC gain over barcode-only inference at 30% dropout.
On ConvergeTree simulations, ablate state mixtures and edit gating at 30% dropout; assess AUROC gain versus barcode-only and sampling-weighted ECE.
Run ConvergeTree v1 ablations across 20 simulated trees at 30% dropout, recording ancestral-pair AUROC and sampling-weighted ECE.
At 30% dropout, ConvergeTree AUROC: 0.83 full, 0.76 barcode-only, 0.79 without mixtures, 0.80 without gating; weighted ECE: 0.038.
Retain state mixtures and edit gating: together they add 0.07 AUROC over barcode-only with weighted ECE 0.038.
With mixtures and gating retained, test inverse-propensity calibration on ConvergeTree v1 at 5:1 lineage imbalance; measure held-out ECE.
ConvergeTree v1 calibration report records held-out ECE of 0.044 with propensity calibration versus 0.091 without under 5:1 lineage imbalance.
Audit the ConvergeTree v1 report by recomputing held-out ECE with lineage-cluster bootstraps and checking propensity-weight sensitivity under 5:1 imbalance.
Lineage-cluster audit found held-out overall ancestral-pair AUROC 0.78 versus 0.76 barcode-only at 30% dropout and 5:1 imbalance.
Lineage-balanced contrastive training with convergent-state hard negatives restores ≥0.05 AUROC gain at 30% dropout and 5:1 sampling imbalance.
On audited ConvergeTree 5:1, 30%-dropout splits, retrain with lineage-balanced contrastive hard negatives; measure AUROC versus barcode-only and ECE.
Infer edit-event phylogenies with explicit barcode-dropout and lineage-capture likelihoods, RNA-velocity transition constraints, and lineage-stratified cross-fitted calibration.
On time-resolved ConvergeTree at 30% dropout, ablate capture and velocity models; compare AUROC and cross-fitted ECE against audited 5:1 baselines.
Using ConvergeTree report's 0.044 ECE baseline, benchmark capture/velocity-ablated edit-event phylogenies for AUROC and ECE at 30% dropout and 5:1 sampling.
ConvergeTree benchmark table records full AUROC/ECE 0.84/0.039, capture-ablated 0.80/0.072, and velocity-ablated 0.79/0.054 at 30% dropout and 5:1 sampling.
Does velocity’s 0.05 AUROC contribution persist when convergent-state velocities are noisy under 5:1 sampling imbalance?
Uncertainty-weighted velocity constraints preserve ≥0.05 ancestral-pair AUROC gain over velocity ablation at 20% direction-flip noise and 5:1 sampling.
Inject 20% velocity-direction flips into ConvergeTree’s 30%-dropout, 5:1 splits; compare uncertainty-weighted ancestry AUROC/ECE with benchmarked full and velocity-ablated models.
At 20% velocity flips, uncertainty-weighted AUROC was 0.84 versus 0.79 velocity-ablated and 0.80 unweighted; ECE was 0.043.
Prioritize uncertainty-weighted edit-event phylogenies for validation: noisy-velocity AUROC 0.84, ECE 0.043; prior state-mixture audit achieved 0.78 AUROC.
Using ConvergeTree’s benchmark table, compare p1 and p2 on held-out trees at 30% dropout and 5:1 sampling using AUROC/ECE.
Held-out 5:1 AUROC/ECE: contrastive p1 0.82/0.047, p2 0.84/0.039, versus barcode-only AUROC 0.76 at 30% dropout.
How does 10% recurrent edit homoplasy affect p2’s ancestry AUROC and calibration under 30% dropout and 5:1 sampling?
Inject 10% recurrent edits into n19’s 20%-velocity-flip ConvergeTree splits; compare p2 AUROC/ECE with homoplasy-free controls.
Train a homoplasy-aware co-edit graph transformer with disentangled transcriptional ancestry features and doubly robust sampling-adjusted calibration.
With convergent states, 10% homoplasy, 30% dropout, and 5:1 sampling, p3 gains ≥0.05 AUROC over barcode-only; ECE ≤0.05.
Benchmark p3 against barcode-only on held-out ConvergeTree trees with convergent states, 10% homoplasy, 30% dropout, and 5:1 sampling; measure AUROC/ECE.
On homoplasy-stressed ConvergeTree, p3 AUROC/ECE were 0.76/0.078 versus barcode-only AUROC 0.73, missing both targets.
Which recurrent-edit patterns cause p3 to merge unrelated lineages, and do these errors explain its ECE of 0.078?
Recurrent edits at high-frequency hotspots falsely connect independent lineages, causing ancestry probabilities above 0.8 and elevated calibration error.
Stratify p3’s ConvergeTree ancestry predictions by hotspot frequency; compare unrelated-lineage merges and high-confidence (>0.8) ECE against nonhotspot edits.
Nonhotspot p3 AUROC/ECE reached 0.84/0.039; hotspot-linked unrelated pairs had 19% false merges versus 4% elsewhere, with >0.8 ECE 0.12.
Can hotspot-frequency-weighted co-edit edges recover ≥0.05 AUROC over barcode-only and ECE ≤0.05 without degrading nonhotspot accuracy?
Downweight hotspot co-edit edges (19% false merges); benchmark AUROC/ECE against p3’s 0.76/0.078, barcode-only AUROC 0.73, and nonhotspot 0.84/0.039.
Hotspot-weighted p3 reached AUROC/ECE 0.80/0.046 versus unweighted 0.76/0.078 and barcode-only AUROC 0.73; nonhotspot AUROC stayed 0.84.
Adopt hotspot-weighted p3: hotspot false merges motivated reweighting; AUROC rose 0.76→0.80, ECE fell 0.078→0.046, preserving nonhotspot AUROC.
Combine dropout-marginalized edit likelihoods, time-series clone frequencies, and convergence-adjusted RNA residuals in lineage-balanced, calibrated Bayesian tree ensembles.
Fit p4 on ConvergeTree with 30% dropout, 10% homoplasy, 5:1 sampling; ablate components and compare AUROC/ECE against hotspot-weighted p3.
Reuse n15’s ConvergeTree splits; fit p4 with 10% homoplasy, ablate clone frequencies and RNA residuals, and measure AUROC/ECE.
ConvergeTree p4 ablation table at 10% homoplasy: full AUROC/ECE 0.83/0.041, without clone frequencies 0.79/0.060, without RNA residuals 0.80/0.052.
Recompute p4’s ablation-table AUROC/ECE on lineage-held-out ConvergeTree trees, bootstrap differences against hotspot-weighted p3, and audit clone-frequency leakage.
Lineage-held-out p4 AUROC/ECE was 0.82/0.044 versus hotspot-weighted p3’s 0.80/0.046; bootstrapped AUROC difference 95% CI: 0.006–0.034.
Advance p4 for homoplasy-stressed validation: AUROC/ECE 0.82/0.044 exceeds p3’s 0.80/0.046; retain p2’s 0.84 noisy-velocity AUROC as comparator.
